page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-96 is a compute-focused instance within the N2D family, engineered for parallel computational workloads requiring high core density. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture, providing 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 96.0 GB total, establishing an exact 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and AVX instructions, though AVX-512 extensions are absent. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Performance benchmarks show top-tier computational output across multi-threaded operations. The instance achieved a top 10% multi-core score of 129,589.51 in stress-ng and an encryption throughput of 102,845.56 in PassMark tests, reflecting the cryptographic acceleration of the AMD architecture. It also ranked in the top 25% for PassMark CPU overall (79,003.93), software compilation using Clang (49,163.0), ray tracing (88,413.0), and Redis SET operations reaching 86.49 million operations per second. General single-core benchmarks and decompression rates placed in the middle tier, aligning with balanced enterprise x86 performance.

From an efficiency standpoint, n2d-highcpu-96 offers high core density at a lower memory ratio, providing strong value for CPU-bound applications without the overhead of unneeded memory capacity. The primary operational tradeoff is the constrained 1.0 GB RAM per vCPU and lack of local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence relies on network storage. This profile is well suited for large-scale distributed compilation, high-concurrency batch processing, continuous integration build matrices, web servers, and parallel computational analytics.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-96 is a compute-intensive virtual machine featuring 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores of a dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processor on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 96.0 GB of system memory, matching a lean 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for CPU-heavy tasks without excess memory costs. There are no included GPUs or local storage devices. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier multi-core compute capability, with top 10% scores in stress-ng multi-threaded processing and PassMark encryption, alongside top 25% marks in Clang software compilation, ray tracing, and Redis throughput. Single-core performance falls within average tiers. The low memory-to-core ratio represents a deliberate tradeoff favoring parallel processing power over in-memory dataset capacity, positioning the instance for distributed software build systems, static web serving clusters, and batch computing pipelines.
